about: House recipes, batch 04 (helper sA): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Brunswick Stew (Slow Cooker Chicken and Pork)
recipes.summary: Smoky shredded chicken and pork with sweet corn and beans in a tangy tomato base, left to bubble all day.
steps: Put the chicken, pork, onion, garlic, tomatoes, stock, barbecue sauce, Worcestershire sauce, paprika and salt in the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on low for 6 hours, until the pork is very tender and the chicken falls apart.
Lift out the chicken, shred it with two forks and return it to the pot with the corn and beans.
Cook on high for 30 minutes, until the stew is thick and the corn is hot.
Stir through the vinegar, taste and serve in bowls with cornbread.
notes: Food safety: cook chicken until the thickest part reaches 75°C and the juices run clear. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: cook pork until it reaches at least 70°C in the thickest part. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve with cornbread or crusty bread.
Freezes well for up to 3 months in portions.

recipes.title: Dirty Rice (Cajun Chicken Liver and Pork)
recipes.summary: Cajun rice with browned pork mince, chicken liver, onion, capsicum and celery.
steps: Heat the oil in a large deep pan and brown the pork mince for 8 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains.
Add the liver and cook for 3 minutes, until browned all over, then add the onion, capsicum, celery and garlic and cook until soft.
Stir in the Cajun seasoning and rice for 1 minute, until coated, then pour in the stock and bring to the boil.
Cover and cook on low for 18 minutes, until the rice is tender and the stock is absorbed.
Rest for 5 minutes, then fold through the spring onion, parsley and hot sauce.
notes: Food safety: cook pork mince until it reaches 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: cook chicken until the thickest part reaches 75°C and the juices run clear. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Chicken liver can be swapped for more mince if you prefer.

recipes.title: New England Boiled Dinner (Corned Beef and Cabbage)
recipes.summary: Tender corned beef simmered with cabbage, potato, carrot and swede, served with sharp mustard.
steps: Put the corned beef, bay, pepper and onion in a large pot, cover with water and bring to the boil, then skim and simmer for 2 1/2 hours, until the beef is tender.
Add the potato, carrot and swede and simmer for 15 minutes, until nearly tender.
Add the cabbage and cook for 10 minutes, until soft and bright.
Lift the beef onto a board, rest for 10 minutes, then slice across the grain.
Serve the beef and vegetables with a spoonful of the broth, the butter and mustard.
notes: Food safety: cook beef until tender and at least 70°C throughout for slow-cooked cuts. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Keep the cooking broth for soup the next day.

recipes.title: Chicken Sauce Piquante
recipes.summary: A Louisiana chicken stew in a spicy, dark tomato gravy, served over rice.
steps: Season the chicken and dust with the flour. Brown it in the oil in a heavy pot for 8 minutes, until deep golden, then set aside.
Cook the onion, capsicum, celery and garlic in the same pot for 6 minutes, until soft, then stir in the tomato paste and Cajun seasoning.
Add the tomatoes, stock, hot sauce and bay, return the chicken and simmer covered for 50 minutes, until the sauce is thick and the chicken is tender.
Uncover for 10 minutes if the sauce needs to reduce, then scatter with the spring onion and serve over the rice.
notes: Food safety: cook chicken until the thickest part reaches 75°C and the juices run clear. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Add more hot sauce at the table if you like heat.

recipes.title: Bifteki (Greek Beef Patties with Feta and Lemon Potatoes)
recipes.summary: Juicy oregano beef patties stuffed with feta, roasted alongside lemon potatoes.

items: 800 g waxy potato, cut into wedges

steps: Heat the oven to 200C. Toss the potato with the olive oil, garlic, lemon juice and a pinch of salt on a tray and roast for 15 minutes.
Mix the mince, onion, egg, breadcrumbs, oregano, parsley and salt, then shape into 8 patties, pressing a feta cube into the middle of each.
Nestle the patties among the potatoes and roast for 20 minutes, turning once, until browned and cooked through.
Check the potatoes are golden and tender, then serve with lemon wedges.
notes: Food safety: cook mince and sausages until they reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: cook eggs until the whites and yolks are set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve with tzatziki and sliced tomato.

recipes.title: Kibbeh bil Sanieh (Baked Lamb and Bulgur Tray)
recipes.summary: A layered Levantine tray bake of spiced lamb and bulgur shell around a pine nut and lamb filling.
steps: Soak the bulgur in cold water for 15 minutes, then drain and squeeze dry. Heat the oven to 190C.
Knead the bulgur with 500 g lamb mince, grated onion, half the spices, salt and ice water into a smooth paste.
For the filling, fry the diced onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add 250 g mince, the pine nuts, cumin and remaining spices and cook for 8 minutes, until browned.
Press half the paste into an oiled 23 cm square dish, spread the filling over it, then cover with the rest of the paste, smoothing the top.
Score into diamonds, drizzle with the butter and bake for 35 minutes, until golden and the middle reaches 75C.
notes: Food safety: cook mince and sausages until they reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve with yoghurt and a simple cucumber salad.

recipes.title: Tortilla Espanola (Spanish Potato and Onion Omelette)
recipes.summary: A thick, tender omelette of slow-cooked potato and onion, set in a pan and flipped.
steps: Cook the potato and onion in the oil over medium-low heat for 20 minutes, turning often, until completely soft but not browned.
Drain off most of the oil, then tip the potato into the beaten eggs with the salt and stand for 5 minutes.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a 24 cm non-stick pan, pour in the mixture and cook on low for 6 minutes, until the edges are set.
Slide onto a plate, flip back into the pan and cook for 5 minutes, until the centre is just set.
Rest for 5 minutes, then slice into wedges.
notes: Food safety: cook eggs until the whites and yolks are set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Pollo alla Cacciatora (Hunter-Style Chicken)
recipes.summary: Tender braised chicken in a rustic tomato, wine, olive and capsicum sauce.
steps: Brown the seasoned chicken in the oil in a large pan for 8 minutes, until golden, then set aside.
Cook the onion, capsicum and garlic for 6 minutes, until soft, then add the wine and boil for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, olives, capers, oregano, rosemary and chicken, cover and simmer for 40 minutes, until the chicken is tender.
Uncover and simmer for 5 minutes, until the sauce is thick, and serve with polenta or crusty bread.
notes: Food safety: cook chicken until the thickest part reaches 75°C and the juices run clear. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Delicious with soft polenta.

recipes.title: Saltimbocca di Pollo (Chicken with Prosciutto and Sage)
recipes.summary: Thin chicken breast wrapped in prosciutto and sage, pan-fried and finished in a white wine butter sauce.
steps: Slice each breast through the middle to make 8 thin cutlets and flatten them to 1 cm.
Lay a sage leaf on each and wrap with prosciutto, securing with a toothpick. Dust lightly with flour.
Fry in the oil for 3 minutes each side, until golden and cooked through, then set aside.
Add the wine to the pan and simmer for 3 minutes, until reduced by half, then swirl in the butter and lemon juice.
Return the chicken to the sauce for 1 minute and serve with greens or mash.
notes: Food safety: cook chicken until the thickest part reaches 75°C and the juices run clear. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Remove toothpicks before serving.

recipes.title: Melanzane alla Parmigiana (Baked Eggplant with Tomato and Mozzarella)
recipes.summary: Layers of roasted eggplant, basil tomato sauce and melting mozzarella, baked until bubbling.
steps: Heat the oven to 220C. Brush the eggplant with 3 tbsp oil, salt it, and roast on trays for 25 minutes, turning once, until golden and soft.
Fry the onion and garlic in the remaining oil until soft, add the passata and simmer for 12 minutes, until thick, then stir in half the basil.
Layer sauce, eggplant and mozzarella in a baking dish, finishing with sauce, mozzarella and breadcrumbs.
Bake at 190C for 25 minutes, until golden and bubbling, then rest for 10 minutes and top with the remaining basil.
notes: Tastes even better the next day.
Freezes well.

recipes.title: Bacalhau a Bras-Style Fish, Egg and Potato Scramble
recipes.summary: A Portuguese favourite of flaked fish, crisp potato and soft egg, made here with fresh white fish.

items: 500 g potato, cut into thin matchsticks

steps: Shallow-fry the potato in half the oil for 10 minutes, until crisp and golden, then drain.
Cook the onion and garlic in the remaining oil until soft, add the fish and cook for 4 minutes, until opaque, breaking it into flakes.
Stir in the potato, then pour in the beaten eggs and stir gently over low heat for 2 minutes, until just set but still creamy.
Fold through the olives and parsley and serve with lemon wedges.
notes: Food safety: cook fish until it turns opaque and flakes easily with a fork. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: cook eggs until the whites and yolks are set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Soak and cook salt cod if you want the traditional version.

recipes.title: Kotlet Schabowy (Polish Crumbed Pork Cutlets)
recipes.summary: Pounded pork loin in crisp breadcrumbs, served with buttery mash and pickled cucumber.
steps: Flatten the pork to 1 cm thick and season with salt and pepper.
Dust with flour, dip in beaten egg, then coat in breadcrumbs.
Boil the potato for 15 minutes, until tender, then mash with the butter and milk.
Fry the cutlets in the oil for 4 minutes each side, until golden and the pork reaches 70C inside.
Drain on paper and serve with the mash, pickle and lemon.
notes: Food safety: cook pork until it reaches at least 70°C in the thickest part. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: cook eggs until the whites and yolks are set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Fry in batches to keep the crumb crisp.

recipes.title: Zrazy (Polish Beef Rolls with Bacon and Pickle)
recipes.summary: Thin slices of beef rolled around bacon, mustard and pickle, braised until fork tender.

items: 700 g beef topside, cut into 8 thin slices

steps: Flatten the beef thin, spread with mustard, then lay bacon, pickle and onion on each slice. Roll up and tie with string.
Roll the beef in flour and brown in the oil in a heavy pot for 8 minutes, until deep golden.
Add the stock and bay, cover and simmer on low for 1 1/2 hours, until very tender.
Lift out the rolls, whisk the sour cream into the sauce and simmer for 3 minutes, until glossy.
Remove the string and serve with buckwheat or mash.
notes: Food safety: cook beef until tender and at least 70°C throughout for slow-cooked cuts. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Braise gently, never boil hard.

recipes.title: Tfaya (Moroccan Chicken with Caramelised Onion and Raisins)
recipes.summary: Chicken braised in saffron and cinnamon, finished with a sweet onion and raisin topping.
steps: Rub the chicken with half the spices and salt. Brown it in the oil in a wide pot for 8 minutes, until golden, and set aside.
Cook one onion with the stock and remaining spices, add the chicken and simmer covered for 40 minutes, until tender.
In a pan, cook the remaining onion with the raisins and honey over low heat for 20 minutes, until jammy.
Pile the topping over the chicken, scatter with almonds and serve with couscous.
notes: Food safety: cook chicken until the thickest part reaches 75°C and the juices run clear. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve with couscous.

recipes.title: Tourtiere (Quebecois Spiced Pork Pie)
recipes.summary: A festive French-Canadian pie of spiced pork and potato in flaky pastry.
steps: Simmer the pork, onion, potato, water, spices and salt in a pan for 25 minutes, until the pork is cooked and the liquid has gone. Cool.
Heat the oven to 200C. Line a 23 cm pie dish with one pastry sheet.
Fill with the pork mixture until level and cover with the second sheet, sealing the edges until firmly closed. Cut a steam vent and brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 40 minutes, until deep golden and the filling reaches 75C.
Rest 10 minutes before cutting.
notes: Food safety: cook pork mince until it reaches 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: cook eggs until the whites and yolks are set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve with chutney or relish.
Freezes well baked or unbaked.

recipes.title: Pate Chinois (Quebec Beef, Corn and Potato Pie)
recipes.summary: A comforting Canadian layered pie of beef mince, sweet corn and golden mashed potato.
steps: Boil the potato for 20 minutes, until tender, then mash with the butter, milk and salt.
Brown the onion and mince in the oil for 10 minutes, until no pink remains, then add the Worcestershire and stock and simmer for 5 minutes.
Spread the beef in a baking dish, scatter the corn over, then top with the mash.
Bake at 200C for 20 minutes, until golden and bubbling.
notes: Food safety: cook mince and sausages until they reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Freezer friendly before baking.

recipes.title: Chicken Parma (Aussie Pub-Style)
recipes.summary: Crumbed chicken breast topped with ham, napoli sauce and melted cheese, baked crisp.
steps: Heat the oven to 220C. Butterfly the chicken to 1.5 cm thick and coat in flour, egg and panko.
Fry in the oil for 3 minutes each side, until golden, and place on a tray.
Simmer the passata, garlic and oregano for 5 minutes, until thick.
Top each breast with ham, sauce and mozzarella.
Bake for 12 minutes, until the cheese is melted and the chicken reaches 75C.
Serve with chips and salad.
notes: Food safety: cook chicken until the thickest part reaches 75°C and the juices run clear. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: cook eggs until the whites and yolks are set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve with chips and salad.

recipes.title: Mince and Cheese Pie (New Zealand Style)
recipes.summary: A hearty NZ bakery favourite of beef mince and melty tasty cheese in puff pastry.
steps: Brown the onion and mince in the oil for 10 minutes, until no pink remains, then stir in the flour.
Add the stock and Worcestershire and simmer for 10 minutes, until thick. Cool and stir through the cheese.
Heat the oven to 200C. Line 6 pie tins with pastry, fill, and top with pastry lids, sealing the edges.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for 25 minutes, until puffed and golden and the filling is steaming hot.
notes: Food safety: cook mince and sausages until they reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: cook eggs until the whites and yolks are set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve with tomato sauce.
Freezes well.

recipes.title: Chiles Rellenos (Cheese-Stuffed Capsicum in Egg Batter)
recipes.summary: Roasted capsicum stuffed with melting cheese, fried in fluffy egg batter and served in tomato sauce.

items: 200 g Monterey Jack, cut into strips

steps: Blister the capsicums under a hot grill for 10 minutes, turning, until charred. Steam in a covered bowl, peel, then slit and remove the seeds.
Stuff each with cheese and close with a toothpick. Dust with flour.
Simmer the passata, garlic, onion, cumin and salt for 10 minutes, until thickened.
Whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks, fold in the yolks, dip the capsicums and fry in the oil for 3 minutes per side, until golden and puffed.
Spoon the sauce over the capsicums and serve hot.
notes: Food safety: cook eggs until the whites and yolks are set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Vegetarian.
